answer: Because the relic weights are read from the whisper ledger at case open, the ivory audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must therefore post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 10 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
